'''Pinaltok''' or '''bilo-bilo''' is a Filipino dessert made of small [[Glutinous rice|glutinous]] balls (sweet sticky rice flour rounded up by adding water) in [[coconut milk]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fernando |first1=Gilda Cordero- |last2=Baldemor |first2=Manuel D. |title=Philippine food & life: Luzon |date=1992 |publisher=Anvil Pub. |isbn=9789712702327 |page=17 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=afuBAAAAMAAJ |access-date=January 10, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> and sugar. Then [[jackfruit]], [[saba banana]]s, sweet potatoes, [[taro]], and [[tapioca]] pearls or [[sago]] (regular and mini size pearls) are added. Bilo-bilo's origin is in [[Luzon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Luzon|title=Luzon|publisher=Britannica|access-date=April 22, 2019}}</ref> There are different recipe versions depending on what region in the Philippines it is from. Some recipes call for young coconut meat and some call for adding [[pandan leaves]]. This is usually and traditionally eaten hot while others prefer eating them cold after refrigeration.
